items.headline: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision
items.blurb: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.
items.text: Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker. The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel, Atlantic Asphalt. The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi". The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering." New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference that all credit in the rescue effort went to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help". "We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said. items.headline: Measles-associated deaths reach 10 in US after two more deaths reported
items.blurb: More than 5,400 confirmed measles cases have been recorded in the US to date this year.
items.text: Pennsylvania and Wisconsin have announced one additional measles-associated death in each state, marking 10 total deaths in the United States linked to the disease this year. The Wisconsin Department of Health Services reported an infant’s death on Friday, while the Pennsylvania Department of Health said that its latest death was an unvaccinated patient who had tested positive for measles. Pennsylvania has logged seven measles-associated deaths, while Wisconsin has reported two. On November 2, New York state said a child had died in the state’s first recorded measles death in more than 30 years. More than 5,400 confirmed measles cases have been recorded in the US to date, according to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the Johns Hopkins University International Vaccine Access Center tracker. The number of confirmed cases as of November 2026 is more than double the 2,289 confirmed cases reported in 2025. The CDC recorded six measles-related deaths, according to figures on its website. Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter , which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October. Five days later, the Atlantic published an article titled “Yet another literary prize winner seems to be AI”, in which the author and journalist Vauhini Vara said the AI-detection software Pangram, which itself uses AI, had deemed the story to be almost completely artificially generated. The Caine prize chair, Ellah Wakatama, said in a statement : “From our detailed investigation, we feel the evidence is clear: The Blue Fighter was human-written. items.headline: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage as it reports broad recovery
items.blurb: Experts say the event is a "stark reminder" of how heavily the world relies on a small group of big tech providers.
items.text: Microsoft has said it is "deeply sorry" for the service outage to its products, including Outlook and Teams, which has caused disruption around the world. Services were broadly recovering by Friday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after issues began. Microsoft said it was making "encouraging progress", but added it does not know when services will fully recover. The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide. Microsoft said it was a technical issue introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and not related to cyber or artificial intelligence agents. Experts said the event was a "stark reminder" of how heavily businesses and vital services rely on a small group of big tech providers. Users began reporting they were having trouble accessing Microsoft 365 products on Thursday. By Friday, the far-reaching issue was affecting institutions from the Japanese government and the Philippines Supreme Court to the Australian spy agency, and trains, hospitals and courts in North America. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said. The health ministry gave the casualty toll, adding more than 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment. Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. items.headline: Algae-based artificial tree to help check air pollution in Guntur
items.blurb: In a first-of-its-kind initiative in Andhra Pradesh, ‘Algae Tree’ draws in polluted air, absorbs carbon dioxide, and releases oxygen through natural photosynthesis
items.text: An ‘Algae Tree’ installed at Gandhi Park in Guntur. A single ‘Algae Tree’ matches the carbon absorption capacity of roughly 20 to 25 mature trees. | Photo Credit: T. Vijaya Kumar In a move to combat air pollution and elevate oxygen levels in urban areas, the Guntur Municipal Corporation (GMC) has unveiled the first ‘Algae Tree’ at Gandhi Park. It is the first-of-its-kind initiative in Andhra Pradesh. Unlike conventional flora, the ‘Algae Tree’ is a specialised, closed-loop, decentralised carbon-capture system powered by solar energy. GMC Commissioner K. Mayur Ashok told The Hindu that this ecological installation marks a milestone in the city's sustainable development initiatives. Developed by Mushroom World Umbrella Limited, the 4.5-metre-tall structure houses a 600-litre transparent chamber filled with high-efficiency microalgae strains. The system draws in surrounding polluted air, absorbs carbon dioxide, and releases oxygen through natural photosynthesis. Equipped with advanced features such as solar panels, an aeration system, LED-assisted illumination, and IoT- enabled sensors monitoring pH, temperature, and airflow, the unit operates efficiently within a compact 1.5 metre footprint. items.headline: Bail can’t become forum to secure maintenance from husband: SC
items.blurb: The Supreme Court has cautioned courts against using bail proceedings to impose conditions requiring a husband to pay maintenance to his wife, underscoring that such matters must be pursued through the appropriate legal forum
items.text: The Supreme Court has cautioned courts against using bail proceedings to impose conditions requiring a husband to pay maintenance to his wife, underscoring that such matters must be pursued through the appropriate legal forum. Setting aside the cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to four members of a family in a matrimonial cruelty and dowry harassment case, a bench of justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar said courts must not turn the process of granting pre-arrest protection into a mechanism for securing maintenance. “A process of bail or anticipatory bail cannot be converted into a forum for grant of maintenance,” emphasised the bench in a recent order, which reinforces the distinction between conditions that may legitimately be attached to bail and the separate remedies available to a spouse seeking financial support during matrimonial litigation. The case arose from a complaint registered in Tamil Nadu under provisions of the Indian Penal Code dealing with cruelty by a husband or his relatives, wrongful confinement and criminal intimidation, besides sections of the Dowry Prohibition Act. items.headline: China's BYD clears import hurdle, looks to accelerate India push
items.blurb: Homologation removes the 2,500-unit import restriction on three models, giving the Chinese carmaker more room to scale its EV business as it enters the luxury market with Denza.
items.text: MUMBAI/NEW DELHI: BYD India has secured regulatory certification for three of its four models, removing the annual 2,500-unit import restriction on those vehicles and giving the Chinese carmaker greater flexibility to meet demand. The move is particularly significant for its fast-selling Sealion 7, as BYD seeks to expand its presence in India's electric passenger vehicle market. "We have four models and three of them are homologated with a certified agency, ARAI, except for Seal," Rajeev Chauhan, executive vice-president at BYD India, told Mint on the sidelines of the launch of the company's luxury brand Denza on Friday. Homologation is the process through which testing agencies such as the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) certify that a vehicle meets the country's technical and safety requirements for road use. Under India's import rules, vehicles with international certification but without Indian homologation can be imported only up to 2,500 units per model annually. Securing Indian homologation removes that restriction. items.headline: Mars bets on India as a top-five growth market, targets $1.2 billion-plus revenue by 2030
items.blurb: The pet-care and snacking giant is expanding manufacturing and investing in technology capabilities as it looks to tap India's growing consumer markets and build a global operating hub.
items.text: HYDERABAD: Mars Inc., the American pet-care and snacking giant, wants India to become one of its five key “rapid growth” markets, betting on the country's expanding snacking and pet-care businesses to drive a sharp increase in revenue. India, already among Mars's top 20 markets, has significant room to grow, with the company targeting revenue of more than $1.2 billion by 2030. “It really ought to be a top 5 market,” Claus Aagaard, global chief financial officer of Mars, told Mint in an interview. The company's India revenue stood at around $600 million in 2025. Mars is stepping up investments in manufacturing and technology to capture that opportunity. It operates seven factories in India and is investing ₹ 1,500 crore in its Hyderabad pet-food facility. It has also partnered with IT services company Genpact to establish a global capability centre (GCC) in the city, which will support technology, analytics and process management across its global operations. “This is a new strategic investment for us to drive innovation around technology and process management,” Aagaard said on the sidelines of the GCC launch.

Claude Duet is even more focused on work than those. It’s also more consumer-friendly than Claude Cowork , which was more consumer-friendly than Claude Code — the coding agent that kicked off a whole hype cycle earlier this year. For specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol, digital transformation is all about giving researchers the tools to test ideas faster, make better-informed decisions, and develop more sustainable materials without compromising performance. Girish Rao, vice president of information technology at Lubrizol, says the company is building a digital foundation that connects business processes, modern data platforms, and cloud infrastructure to support its research and development (R&D) teams. Their goal is to combine decades of accumulated technical data with the deep expertise of chemists and engineers who understand customer needs as well as the physical constraints of their work. Data scientists can help identify patterns, test new hypotheses, and model possibilities before researchers conduct physical experiments. items.blurb: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially…
items.text: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.” Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy. When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, explicitly opposed the bill and wrote that its mandates for chip tracking were “new, untested, and potentially infeasible.”

items.text: MeitY has sought details from Pronto, Snabbit and Urban Company on their collection and use of gig workers’ video and sensor data for physical AI training The move highlights growing government concerns around worker consent, consumer privacy, data security and the transfer of Indian training data to overseas AI developers The ministry has sought information on companies’ data collection SOPs and consent safeguards, as India’s physical AI data ecosystem expands The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has sought details from home services platforms, including Pronto, Snabbit and Urban Company’s InstaHelp, over the collection of first-person video and sensor data from gig workers for training physical AI models. As per a report by ET , a meeting chaired by MeitY secretary S Krishnan yesterday brought together senior executives from the quick home services platforms and other technology and robotics companies to discuss concerns around workers’ consent, consumer privacy and data sovereignty. Officials are concerned that recordings of everyday household activities could infringe workers’ rights, compromise consumer privacy and pose risks to national data security.
